PDF pp.7–8,19 Figure 2: five evaluations sample 128 of 231 unseen fixed-reference OLMo3-100M interventions; 16 arrive per round, three selections per round over eight rounds, unselected candidates remain. Initial 244-record history is outside the selection budget. Mean final best gain improves 15.8%/11.6%; nAULC values are 85.26/98.26/94.34 for zero/in/cross histories, normalized per matched Arrival Oracle.

PDF pp.3,8,17 Figure 3: 13 backbones on one OLMo3-100M panel have Spearman ranges −.362 to .621 without history versus .638 to .896 with history. LOW→MAX without records .609→.648 is not monotonic scaling; the plotted best no-record setting is XHIGH. LOW plus records .892 exceeds all no-record settings on that panel only.

PDF pp.7,10,15: approximate API cost $6.3 for 16 forecasts is 5% of one representative $127 experiment at the paper’s assumed $3/H100-hour. This is not a measured total-cost saving; 171,862 hours producing records, retained-record context and future acquisition costs matter. PDF pp.10,16–19: release review is future tense; condensed prompt, TF–IDF baselines and conditional bootstrap details are specified. llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant empirical study of reusable experimental memory for language-model research agents. Matched record conditions and held-out transfer groups support substantial forecasting and budgeted-selection gains. The contribution is narrower than a general research world model: transfer is restricted to small autoregressive pretraining variants, two transfer intervals include zero, Marin selection worsens, and multi-round discovery uses a fixed measured candidate pool. Initial-record costs, intervention variance and artifact availability remain unresolved; gains are not proof of open-ended self-improvement or total compute savings.

The contribution is narrower than a general research world model: transfer is restricted to small autoregressive pretraining variants, two transfer intervals include zero, Marin selection worsens, and multi-round discovery uses a fixed measured candidate pool. Initial-record costs, intervention variance and artifact availability remain unresolved; gains are not proof of open-ended self-improvement or total compute savings.
llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這是高度相關的語言模型研究代理實證工作，展示既有實驗記憶可重用。相同紀錄條件對照與遷移保留群組支持預測及預算內選擇的改善，但結論比通用研究世界模型狹窄：遷移限小型自回歸預訓練、兩個區間含零、Marin 選擇變差，多輪探索也使用固定且已有量測的候選池。初始紀錄成本、干預變異與可取得產物仍未解決，不能把增益當成開放式自我改進或總算力節省的證明。
llm_evaluation.scope_assessment: In scope: general language-model experimental forecasting, in-context learning and research-agent selection; not a pure domain application.

primary_link.title: Language Models as AI Research World Models

papers.summary: AI research agents automate the cycle of proposing, implementing, and evaluating experiments, opening a path toward recursive self-improvement. Yet their ability to propose experiments outpaces their capacity to execute them in real environments, making outcome prediction a key capability for sustained self-improvement under limited experimental budgets. We investigate language models as Research World Models (RWMs), which predict the outcomes of candidate interventions across research environments. Our evaluation draws on over 2,600 experimental records from nine research environments spanning pretraining, post-training, and inference, representing more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours of experimentation. Research knowledge acquired from real experimental experience improves RWM predictions of unseen interventions within the same environment (Spearman +0.27), and can be reused across environments. For example, using only pretraining experience from OLMo3, Marin, and Nanochat, an RWM reduces selection regret in the Qwen3 environment by 78% compared with zero-experience setting. These benefits extend to multi-round Autoresearch under a fixed selection budget: RWMs with in-env and cross-env research knowledge increase the best gain achieved by 15.8% and 11.6%, respectively. Ablations across 13 language models used as RWMs show that adding research knowledge can improve intervention ranking more than changing models or increasing reasoning effort alone. These findings support language models as RWMs and motivate accumulating experimental data for future RWM training.
papers.summary_en: Frozen LLMs use experimental records to forecast intervention gains. Across five in-environment tests, mean Spearman rises from .506 to .774; transfer is tested only on small autoregressive pretraining variants and worsens selection on Marin. Fixed-pool multi-round selection improves final best gain by 15.8% with in-environment records and 11.6% with cross-environment records. Single splits, incomplete uncertainty and excluded initial-record costs limit claims about open-ended research and total savings.
papers.summary_zh:
研究代理很容易提出實驗，真正訓練與測試卻昂貴。本文讓參數固定的語言模型讀取環境、程式修改與既有實驗紀錄，預測相對基準的效果，再挑選值得執行的候選。這裡的「世界模型」預測的是一次完整實驗的增益，不是模擬所有中間狀態；學習也透過上下文完成，沒有重新訓練模型。

作者累積九種環境、二千六百五十三筆實驗，涵蓋預訓練、後訓練及推論。同環境的五組測試中，加入紀錄後平均 Spearman 排序相關由零點五零六升至零點七七四；跨環境測試則只涵蓋五種小型自回歸預訓練配置。Qwen3 的前三名選擇遺憾約降七成八，但 Marin 的選擇結果反而變差，不能說遷移普遍有效。

多輪測試在固定候選池中，每輪選三個、共二十四次；同環境與跨環境紀錄令最終最佳增益分別提高百分之十五點八與十一點六。這不等於模型準確率增加同樣百分點，也未計入取得初始紀錄的成本。單一資料切分、部分信賴區間含零、缺乏逐項實驗變異與尚未核實的程式資料限制了結論。價值在於證明實驗檔案能改善研究排序，距離開放式自我改進及總成本優勢仍有待驗證。

links.title: Trajectory-Guided Fault Localization for Agent Skill Evolution

evidence: PDF pp.2–4/Sections 1–2 and Equations 1–3: model/harness remain fixed; only skill artifacts evolve. The stated objective is held-out-task success, not improvement of model weights. A skill spans SKILL.md plus references/scripts; an edit site may cover several files and skills.

PDF pp.4–6/Figures 1–3: the mcp-builder illustration traces a wrong in-memory SQLite connection and missed stdin-close shutdown check to workflow/reference sections, adds coordinated instructions and tests, and reports transfer to a third held-out document-retrieval task. This is an explanatory example, not a separate large validation dataset.

PDF pp.6–9/Section 4.1–4.2/Equations 4–9: trajectories are semantically normalized with an LLM and hierarchical clustering. Every action in a failed run receives failure coverage; successful-run actions can also receive failure coverage if an LLM says they introduced a later-recovered error. Each run contributes at most once to each sign of coverage. These labels are model judgments, not deterministic ground-truth blame.

PDF pp.7–9: a local h-step window is used to distinguish introducing from revealing errors, but no numeric h is specified. Adjacent-loop weights are 2(current count+1)/(current+previous count+2), applied separately to failure/success counts before cross-task aggregation; adjusted counts are not cumulatively added across loops. Ochiai-like scores rank top-n actions, not calibrated defect probabilities.

PDF pp.8–10/Sections 4.2–4.3: historical changes are interpreted as effects of the preceding revision despite stochastic executions. Fixed model/harness alone does not remove sampling or context confounding. An LLM narrows skills→artifacts→line ranges, drafts proposals, checks evidence/conflicts/success cases, and consolidates a patch; this selection stage is not a formal replay-based non-regression guarantee.

PDF pp.10–11/Section 5.1: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 through Claude Code is used for execution and throughout evolution. Default m=3; SWE uses three loops, CannBot five, with top-10 actions. SWE’s 49 skills each have ten tasks split into odd/even-ID folds, swapped as evolution/evaluation; CannBot has one LLM-selected 15/15 split with ten Level-1 and five Level-2 tasks per set.

PDF pp.10–11/metrics/Table 1: pass@3 means at least one success among three actual trials; pass3 means all three pass; trial accuracy is the proportion of successful individual trials. SkillMorph SWE counts are 468/490 pass@3=95.51%, 1356/1470 trials=92.24%, and 433/490 all-three=88.37%. These must not be conflated with pass@1, three independent evolution replications or probabilities of perfect future execution.

PDF pp.11–12/Table 1: original SWE scores are 82.45/75.44/67.96%; CAP-Evolve 92.24/89.39/84.90%; SkillMorph 95.51/92.24/88.37% for pass@3/trial/all-three respectively. Relative gains over originals are 15.84%,22.27%,30.03%; absolute improvements are 13.06,16.80,20.41 percentage points. Against CAP-Evolve they are 3.27,2.86,3.47 points, corresponding to 16 more tasks solved at least once, 42 trials and 17 tasks solved consistently.

PDF pp.11–12/Table 1: CannBot SkillMorph is 14/15 tasks successful in every trial, hence all three metrics equal 93.33%. CAP-Evolve ties pass@3 at 93.33% but achieves 84.44% trial accuracy and 73.33% all-three. The original all-three score doubles from 7/15 to 14/15; this is a 100% relative gain, not 100% final success or a 100-percentage-point gain.

PDF pp.12–13/Figure 4: compared with original SWE skills, 126 tasks improve and nine regress; among 333 originally all-three-passing tasks, 327 remain all-three passing. Across 98 skill/fold instances, 60 improve, 33 remain and five regress. CannBot improves seven of 15 tasks with zero observed regressions in this sample, which is not a universal safety guarantee.

PDF pp.13–14/Figure 5/Table 2: intermediate evolution loops can regress. Removing localization lowers SWE all-three from 88.37 to 82.24 and CannBot from 93.33 to 60.00. Single-run lowers SWE pass@3 to 90.20 and CannBot to 80.00; this ablation also uses fewer task executions. Removing history retains CannBot pass@3=93.33 but lowers all-three to 80.00; it removes both reweighting and proposal-history context, not an isolated test of the equation.

PDF pp.11 and 13/efficiency: average evolution loop is about 49 minutes per SWE skill and 127 for CannBot with task-level parallelization; framework subtasks account for approximately 28.8 and 29.0 minutes. Downstream average execution is 16.45→16.35 minutes on SWE and 141.55→87.07 on CannBot. These are wall-clock timings under reported environments, not token/dollar budgets or an amortized end-to-end net saving after all evolution costs.

PDF p.14/Section 6: practical work covers 63 operators and reports six developer-accepted skill-revision PRs, without independently reviewed PR links here. The 123.63→72.81 minute reduction (41.11%) is restricted to tasks passing correctness with both skill versions; no denominator for that subset or uncertainty interval is reported.

PDF p.14/Section 6: among 1788 case-level measurements for correct kernels, 64.26% achieve ≥0.6× reference speed, 54.14% ≥0.8×, and 44.18% match/exceed reference (≥1×). The first two thresholds include slower kernels. These measurements are not 1788 independent operators and do not quantify a before/after causal speedup from skill revision.

PDF p.15/Figure 6/Discussion: n=1 gives pass@3 90.00% but all-three only 69.39%; n=5/10 improves consistency and larger n adds little. Twenty-one tasks fail all three held-out trials with both original and opposite-fold-evolved skills; five later succeed at least once when they themselves provide evolution feedback. This task-specific analysis is exploratory, not extra held-out generalization evidence.

PDF pp.6–16/implementation/threats and full references pp.16–20: two benchmarks, one backbone, fixed task splits and no reported full-pipeline repetition confidence intervals limit external/statistical claims. A three-trial evaluation helps characterize execution consistency but does not measure variation of learned revisions across independent evolution runs. Complete prompts, clustering settings, immutable skill revisions, chosen CannBot task IDs and raw execution artifacts were not provided and checked in this packet.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A strong fit for agent-engineering interests, with a coherent and inspectable bridge from execution evidence to persistent skill edits. The evaluation goes beyond a single success rate by separating at-least-one success, individual-trial accuracy and all-three consistency, and reports real regressions rather than asserting monotonic improvement. Broad SWE gains and localization ablations are encouraging, but the strongest-baseline margin, tiny CannBot sample and single-model setup warrant calibration. Historical associations and LLM-mediated localization are not causal defect proofs, and equal task executions do not imply equal optimization compute. Incomplete artifact detail, unverified accepted PRs and conditional industrial timing results constrain replication and deployment claims.
llm_evaluation.rationale_en: A strong fit for agent-engineering interests, with a coherent and inspectable bridge from execution evidence to persistent skill edits. The evaluation goes beyond a single success rate by separating at-least-one success, individual-trial accuracy and all-three consistency, and reports real regressions rather than asserting monotonic improvement. Broad SWE gains and localization ablations are encouraging, but the strongest-baseline margin, tiny CannBot sample and single-model setup warrant calibration. Historical associations and LLM-mediated localization are not causal defect proofs, and equal task executions do not imply equal optimization compute. Incomplete artifact detail, unverified accepted PRs and conditional industrial timing results constrain replication and deployment claims.
llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 與代理工程需求高度契合，將執行證據連到持久技能修改的位置，流程連貫且可檢視。評估區分至少一次成功、單次試驗正確率與三次皆成功，也明列退步，沒有只用單一平均掩蓋問題。SWE 的廣泛增益與定位消融值得注意，但最強基準差距、CannBot 小樣本和單模型設定要求審慎。歷史關聯與 LLM 定位不是缺陷因果證明，相同任務執行數也不等於相同優化算力。產物細節不足、PR 未獨立核實及工業時間結果的條件式子集，限制重現與部署結論。
llm_evaluation.scope_assessment: In scope: LLM coding-agent skill evolution and trajectory-grounded procedural guidance; hardware kernels are one software-engineering test domain.

primary_link.title: Trajectory-Guided Fault Localization for Agent Skill Evolution

papers.summary: Agent skills provide reusable guidance for code agents, but incomplete or unsuitable guidance can impair task execution. To reduce the manual effort of skill refinement, recent approaches use LLMs to generate revisions from execution feedback. However, grounding these revisions in explicit behavioral evidence remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose SkillMorph, a skill-evolution approach based on trajectory-guided fault localization in agent skills. Its core idea is to link execution evidence to specific skill contents before generating revisions. Specifically, SkillMorph compares failure and success evidence in abstracted trajectories across repeated runs and tasks, incorporating changes between evolution loops to identify suspicious actions. It then uses these suspicious actions to localize edit sites in the skills and generate corresponding revisions. Experiments on SWE-Skills-Bench and CannBot show that the skills evolved by SkillMorph consistently achieve higher trial-level accuracy and execution consistency than the original skills and those from four existing skill-evolution methods. We have also applied SkillMorph to automated kernel generation with an AI operator-development team, which has accepted 6 skill-revision pull requests.
papers.summary_en:
When an agent fails, defective skill guidance must be distinguished from incidental behavior. SkillMorph first abstracts repeated execution traces into state transitions. It compares action coverage in successful, failed and recovered executions, adjusts it using changes from the previous evolution loop, and aggregates across tasks. An LLM then maps suspicious actions to files and line ranges, proposes coordinated skill edits, and selects a consolidated revision.

Across 490 SWE-Skills-Bench tasks with three evaluation trials each, trial-level accuracy rises from 75.44% to 92.24%, and the proportion passing all three trials rises from 67.96% to 88.37%. The trial-accuracy gain over the strongest baseline, CAP-Evolve, is 2.86 percentage points. On 15 CannBot tasks, SkillMorph solves 14 in all three trials; CAP-Evolve also solves 14 at least once, so this comparison primarily demonstrates greater consistency.

Read the metric definitions and fold split before the ablations and regression counts. Nine tasks and five skill instances still regress. The study uses one model throughout and does not report uncertainty across independently repeated evolution pipelines. Action abstraction, error labeling and revision selection also depend on LLM judgments. In the practical case study, the 41.11% completion-time reduction is restricted to tasks passing with both original and evolved skills, and only 44.18% of kernel measurements meet or exceed reference performance. All 20 pages and figures/tables were read. The contribution is an inspectable skill-revision workflow; fault localization remains an inference requiring validation, and six reportedly accepted pull requests do not establish universal effectiveness or safety.
papers.summary_zh:
代理失敗時，問題可能出在技能文件，也可能只是一次偶發行為。SkillMorph 不直接請模型重寫整份技能，而先把多次執行濃縮成狀態轉移，比較動作在成功、失敗與自行修復過程中的出現情形，再加入前輪變化及跨任務證據，定位應修改的檔案與行範圍，協調多份技能一起修訂。

在 SWE-Skills-Bench 的四百九十題、每題三次評估中，單次試驗成功率由 75.44% 升至 92.24%，三次皆成功的比例由 67.96% 升至 88.37%。相較最強基準 CAP-Evolve，前者提升 2.86 個百分點。CannBot 十五題有十四題三次皆過，但至少成功一次的題數與 CAP-Evolve 相同，優勢主要是穩定性。

先看指標定義與跨折切分，再讀消融及退步統計：方法仍使九題、五個技能實例退步，不能保證不破壞舊能力。所有實驗使用同一模型，未報獨立演化重跑的不確定性；動作抽象、錯誤判定和修訂選擇也依賴 LLM。實務案例的 41.11% 省時只涵蓋新舊技能都通過的任務，且僅 44.18% 核心測量達到參考性能。全文二十頁與圖表已讀。它提供可追查的技能修訂流程，但故障定位仍是待驗證的推論，不能把六個已接受 PR 當成普遍成效或安全保證。

links.title: All Verdicts are Not Equal: Rethinking LLM Judge Reliability

evidence: PDF pp.4,11,17 Table 9: four fixed samples of 100 pairs, six judges, five pairwise formats, two orders, ten repetitions; two reasoning models lack temperature controls. Additional .5/1.0 sweeps use four judges only. The design implies 240,000 nominal Ts=0 pairwise calls, not 240,000 independent examples or a verified successful-call log.

PDF pp.3–5 Eq.3/Table 1: forced binary verdicts and equally weighted orders yield A=(1−phi)A_dec+phi/2, hence A<=1−phi/2. Gemini-2.0-Flash VF-XML/JudgeBench has C=100%, phi=98%, A=51%, T=2%. This is one configuration and finite ten-repeat consistency, not a universally deterministic model.

PDF p.3 Eq.4 and pp.17–18 Appendix G: T_joint=Pr(N and P and R), whereas T_closed=C(A−phi/2) uses A2 conditional-independence equalities. Reviewer derivation: if B=1[P and R], then T_joint−T_closed=Cov(N,B); without a sign condition either direction is possible. Table 10 is empirical, not a proof of a global lower bound, and several printed gap intervals include positive values.

PDF p.5 Table 1 and p.12 Table 4: Gemini-2.5-Pro/JudgeBench Direct A=63.5,T=28.9,phi=56.0 versus VF-JSON A=88.5,T=77.5,phi=6.9. Changes are +25.0 and +48.6 percentage points, not relative percentages. All 120 printed T cells were arithmetically checked within rounding tolerance.

PDF pp.7–8 Table 2: G-Eval versus Direct improves JudgeBench T for Gemini-Pro, Gemini-Flash and Claude, but lowers GPT-5.2, GPT-4o and Llama; LLMBar improves Gemini-Flash and Llama, lowers both GPTs and Gemini-Pro, and ties Claude at printed precision. The largest +49.0 pp example exceeds the largest format dispersion 48.6 pp by only .4 pp, with no reported interval for that comparison.

PDF p.7 Section 5.6 says FLASK leaves T lower than Direct for five of six judges. Table 2 actually shows three of six decreases on JudgeBench, with Gemini-Pro 28.9→37.7, Gemini-Flash 32.2→37.9 and Claude 49.3→51.1 increasing; LLMBar decreases for all six. The sentence is not supported as stated.

PDF pp.6–7,11 Figure 3/Table 3: temperature analysis averages a collapsed three-format view (48 judge-format-dataset cells); reported mean consistency falls 12.1 pp and bias-adjusted capability changes +.3 pp. Bands are interquartile ranges, not confidence intervals, and reasoning models are excluded.

PDF p.13 Tables 5/6: judge-by-dataset variation is 28.1% of T ANOVA variance. G-study measures verdict direction, not directly correctness or trustworthiness; pair-by-judge interaction therefore shows item-specific disagreement, not alone calibrated item reliability.

PDF pp.14–16: Direct permits 32 output tokens while structured formats allow 4096. G-Eval adds task-specific ranked rubrics and ordinal scores; FLASK uses four independent calls and partly different criteria. These are not interventions isolating only holistic versus decomposed reasoning. G-Eval text permits ties but winner schema forces A/B; four-way FLASK vote can tie and no tie-break rule is supplied.

PDF pp.17–18 Table 10: format/temperature aggregation and CI method are unspecified. MT-Bench Llama T_closed .58 cannot be reproduced as the equal five-format Ts=0 mean (.5464) or any printed per-format value (max .566); Flash .51 differs from .442 mean. This is unresolved reporting ambiguity, not a claim of fabricated data.

PDF pp.1–18: no exact backend model snapshots, raw verdict table or unambiguous parser/invalid-output handling is provided. C is captioned deterministic across ten reps, but precise how-to for reducing non-unanimous repetitions to order flip/correctness statistics remains unclear. Referenced studies were not independently read.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A useful, highly relevant stress test showing that repeatability is not correctness or order robustness. The controlled prompt/order grid supports the core diagnostic concern, but the proposed T is only a closed-form proxy under A2, not an assumption-free joint probability or universal conservative bound. Holistic rubric results are mixed, the FLASK comparison sentence conflicts with its table, and sparse uncertainty, unresolved aggregation and operational details weaken the stronger recommendations. Treat this as evidence to audit multiple reliability axes, not as a validated scalar replacement for accuracy.
llm_evaluation.rationale_en: A useful, highly relevant stress test showing that repeatability is not correctness or order robustness. The controlled prompt/order grid supports the core diagnostic concern, but the proposed T is only a closed-form proxy under A2, not an assumption-free joint probability or universal conservative bound. Holistic rubric results are mixed, the FLASK comparison sentence conflicts with its table, and sparse uncertainty, unresolved aggregation and operational details weaken the stronger recommendations. Treat this as evidence to audit multiple reliability axes, not as a validated scalar replacement for accuracy.
llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這是高度相關且有實用價值的壓力測試，說明重問一致不等於正確或不受順序影響。相同題目的提示與順序交叉比較支持核心診斷，但新指標只有在 A2 下才等於聯合機率，並非無條件可靠率或普遍保守下界。整體規準的效果混合，FLASK 比較句與表格矛盾，主要結果缺不確定性、聚合及操作細節未清，削弱較強建議。適合用來提醒分軸稽核，尚不足以把新單一分數視為已驗證的準確率替代品。
llm_evaluation.scope_assessment: In scope: general language-model judging and evaluation methodology, not a pure domain application.

primary_link.title: All Verdicts are Not Equal: Rethinking LLM Judge Reliability

papers.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge is the standard paradigm for NLP evaluation, yet its systemic reliability remains poorly understood despite being widely treated as a deterministic ground truth. We present a comprehensive reliability audit, stresstesting six frontier models across four benchmarks, five prompt formats, two presentation orders, three sampling temperatures, and ten repetitions per condition. Our empirical analysis reveals severe vulnerabilities: verdicts change across identical replications at temperature zero, position-order swaps flip the majority of verdicts on challenging tasks, and the most deterministic judge achieves perfect consistency by trivially repeating incorrect verdicts, agreeing with ground truth only 51% of the time. To formalize these multi-faceted failure modes, we introduce the trustworthy verdict rate (T ), a unified metric capturing the joint probability that an evaluation is reproducible, order-invariant, and accurate. UsingT , we derive a theoretical upper bound on accuracy imposed by position bias and show that reliability is item-specific rather than modellevel. Finally, we demonstrate that shifting from pairwise win-rate to holistic rubric scoring improves trustworthiness more than any single-format prompting intervention, offering an actionable framework for robust NLP evaluation.
papers.summary_en: The audit tests six LLM judges on 100 pairs from each of four English benchmarks. One JudgeBench configuration is 100% consistent across ten repetitions yet flips on 98% of order swaps and is only 51% accurate. The proposed closed-form trustworthy rate equals the true joint rate only under an independence assumption; its lower-bound claim is not general. G-Eval also has mixed effects, improving three of six judges on JudgeBench. Missing uncertainty and aggregation details limit stronger conclusions.
papers.summary_zh:
語言模型裁判每次都給相同答案，就值得相信嗎？本文把可靠性拆成重問是否一致、交換兩個答案的位置是否改判，以及是否符合標準答案。作者從四個英文基準各取一百組比較，測試六種裁判、五種提示格式、兩種順序與每條件十次重問；只有四種可調溫模型參與額外溫度測試。

最醒目的例子是 Gemini-2.0-Flash 在 JudgeBench 的先裁決 XML 格式：十次重問的一致率達百分之百，換位改判率卻為百分之九十八，準確率只有百分之五十一。這清楚說明穩定重複不等於正確，也支持評測同時報告順序與提示敏感度。

作者另用一致率乘上扣除位置因素的準確率，形成「可信裁決率」。但它等於真正聯合可靠機率需要獨立性假設；附錄的有限樣本比較不能證明它永遠是保守下界。整體規準評分也不是通用解方：表二在 JudgeBench 的六種裁判有三升三降，LLMBar 則二升、三降、一持平；文中對分項投票退步比例另有與表格不符的敘述。這份研究有實用診斷價值，但每基準僅一百題、缺少主要比較的不確定性，以及重複裁決與平手處理細節未清，使新指標與改善建議仍需審慎採用。

links.title: Structure Tax: How Structured Output affects LLMs Performance

evidence: PDF pp.3–5, Sections 3–4 and Table 1: five models, four benchmarks, two structured families with two orderings plus free form; mean accuracy and standard deviation are reported over five independent runs. Counting Table 1 gives 13/20 best cells to reasoning-first formats, three to answer-first and three to free form plus one additional answer-first Spider cell; equivalently 13 reasoning-first, four answer-first, three free-form winners.

PDF p.5/Table 1: GSM8K Llama-3.1-8B XML answer-first 10.98±2.66 versus reasoning-first 83.53±2.58; Gemma3-4B 10.98±2.13 versus 87.06±2.34. These are percentages, not relative improvements. JSON is not interchangeable: Claude GSM8K answer-first 96.13 exceeds reasoning-first 87.79, though its XML reasoning-first reaches 97.65.

PDF p.5/Table 1: LogicBench answer-first wins for Claude (XML 88.40 versus free form 87.60), Llama (JSON 76.00) and Gemma (JSON 69.40). Spider free form wins for Gemini, Llama and Gemma; Gemma XML reasoning-first is 63.35 versus 70.21 free form. These contradict blanket claims that reasoning-first never harms or that every low-structure task benefits from the same ordering.

PDF pp.11–13/A.1–A.2: free-form MMLU says solve the MCQ and calibration says answer directly, whereas XML explicitly includes a reasoning field; free-form LogicBench and Spider do not explicitly request a rationale. Within-family order contrasts are cleaner than attributing every free-form versus structured difference to delimiters alone. No grammar-constrained decoder or production schema enforcement is demonstrated.

PDF p.13/A.3/Table 3: authors report zero structured-schema violations but a Gemma3-4B free-form parser bug producing 29.8% empty extraction on MMLU and 45.2% on LogicBench. No explicit correction/rerun accounting states how these failures affect Table 1 or calibration populations; do not reinterpret parsing errors as model reasoning failures or silently repair the reported accuracy.

PDF pp.5–6/Figure 2/Table 2: XML reasoning-first reduces ECE in many cells but not GPT-4o GSM8K (delta −0.008) or MMLU (−0.028), nor Claude Spider (−0.028) or Gemma Spider (−0.061). Table 2 confidence–correctness correlations remain low, approximately 0.115–0.396; aggregate calibration is not reliable instance-level self-verification.

PDF pp.14–15/C.2/Table 5: prose claims absolute prompting has lower/equal ECE in 6 of 8 model–dataset pairs. The displayed table contains ten pairs; absolute ECE is lower only for GPT-4o and Claude on both tasks (4/10), while relative is lower for Gemini, Llama and Gemma (6/10). The prose direction and denominator are not supported by its table. Brier columns are relative-only, so a between-strategy Brier advantage cannot be calculated from those columns.

PDF pp.13–15/A.4/C.3/Table 6: logit confidence comes from a separate answer-only prompt, while verbal confidence is requested in formatted/free-form responses. The comparison therefore changes elicitation context, not just uncertainty readout. Llama MMLU Spearman −0.049 and Gemma 0.024 are nonsignificant; general model-size claims remain limited.

PDF p.16/Figures 4–5: Figure 4 caption claims Gemma free-form accuracy below 26% on MMLU/LogicBench and Llama LogicBench 23%, whereas plotted points are around 60%/44% and 69%. Figure 5 caption cites Llama LogicBench ECE 0.703, Gemma LogicBench 0.645 and Gemma MMLU 0.721, while the visible panel labels read 0.255, 0.462 and 0.359. These are unreconciled figure-caption errors; calibration prompts also differ from Table 1 accuracy prompts, so cross-experiment accuracy differences alone are not automatically errors.

PDF pp.16–18/D.1–D.2: n=200 examples per dataset are partitioned into correct/incorrect groups. Cross-group CKA is written using n-by-n Gram matrices, but unequal group sizes and row correspondence between different examples are not specified. Low CKA is not itself a classification-separation or causal-mechanism proof. Within-group inter-layer CKA is a different, directly described computation.

PDF pp.17–22/D.2/Figures 6–9: difference is defined as correct minus incorrect, and colorbars map blue to negative and red to positive; the reading guide says blue means the correct group has higher similarity, reversing that sign. This affects interpretation of the difference plots and is retained as an author-reporting inconsistency.

PDF pp.7 and 23/Section 6.2/D.3/Figures 3 and 10/Table 7: logistic probes predict the model’s own selected option at the token before its answer letter, with L2 C=1 and five-fold cross-validation. Table 7 correctly separates full preceding reasoning under R,A from none under A,R; surrounding prose inconsistently calls both the end of a reasoning field. Figure 3 marks peak gaps +0.64/+0.70, while main prose calls 0.64/0.70 absolute balanced accuracies. No causal intervention establishes that these readouts prove faithful reasoning or correctness.

PDF p.23/D.4/Figure 10: the Gemma Spider panel labels freeform/R,A mid-layer CKA as 3.38× and the free-form curve lies mostly above R,A, contrary to its caption/prose claim of the same Spider reversal seen in Llama. The plotted answer-first/R,A ratio is 0.66×, a distinct comparison that should not be substituted for freeform/R,A.

PDF pp.8 and 24/E/Tables 8–9: MMLU median reasoning length is 33 words for JSON A,R versus 121 for XML R,A; GSM8K spans 108–127 words. Across 80 aggregate model/task/format cells, overall length–accuracy r=0.04 and JSON A,R r=−0.73. Correlations across such heterogeneous cells do not show that a short output reliably diagnoses post-hoc rationalization for an individual example.

PDF pp.24–25/F/Table 10/Figure 11: role paraphrase, casing and whitespace perturbations preserve R,A>A,R on GSM8K for GPT-4o and Llama. Smallest displayed pair gap is 37 percentage points; greatest within-cell spread is 11.5. This is a focused two-model/one-task robustness check, not universality; sampling size and variation of this ablation are not clearly stated, and all 2×2×4 displayed pair comparisons total 16 rather than the main text’s 24 combinations.

PDF pp.9 and 13–14/Limitations/A.4/B: only four coarse task families, two open models for representations, two orderings, prompting rather than training, and no multilingual evaluation. Sizes are GSM8K 1319, LogicBench 500, MMLU 1531 and Spider 1030. Temperature zero is called deterministic despite nonzero five-run standard deviations; run variation source, API revisions and exact data membership are not fully documented.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant practical study with a useful central distinction: structure and answer order should not be conflated. The large GSM8K gaps and the fact that reasoning-first wins 13/20 configurations merit attention, while LogicBench and SQL counterexamples should remain visible. Scientific confidence is reduced substantially by admitted free-form extraction failures without corrected accounting, a confidence-elicitation conclusion contradicted by its own table, several figure/prose inconsistencies, and an underspecified cross-group CKA analysis. Predicted-label probes and four heterogeneous task families do not demonstrate a universal causal mechanism or an intrinsic-structure law. Treat the paper as a motivating benchmark report for local replication, with complete source availability distinct from methodological reliability.

primary_link.title: Structure Tax: How Structured Output affects LLMs Performance

papers.summary: Deploying large language models in production often requires constraining outputs to structured formats such as JSON or XML, and prior work treats the resulting accuracy loss as an inherent `structure tax'. We re-examine this claim by evaluating a battery of models, datasets and schemas, measuring task accuracy, confidence calibration, and hidden-state geometry. The tax turns out to depend on schema design rather than on structure per se: reasoning-first field ordering matches or exceeds free-form accuracy, while answer-first ordering causes steep drops, particularly in smaller models. Format sensitivity scales inversely with a task's own structural constraints, and schemas that preserve reasoning order also improve calibration with CKA showing greater separability between correct and incorrect representations in middle transformer layers. Our findings indicate that properly designed structured formats can match or exceed free-form performance, reframing the critical question from `whether to structure' to `how to structure' for optimal reasoning preservation.
papers.summary_en:
Does requiring JSON or XML necessarily reduce language-model accuracy? This study separates output family from field order, comparing reasoning-first, answer-first and free-form prompts across five models and four benchmarks, then examining confidence calibration and hidden representations. Its practical contribution is to highlight when an answer is generated, rather than treating every structured format as equivalent.

Reasoning-first formats win 13 of the 20 model–task pairs in Table 1. On GSM8K, answer-first XML scores 10.98% for both Llama and Gemma, versus 83.53% and 87.06% with reasoning first. However, answer-first formats win for three LogicBench models, and structured SQL generation can regress. These results do not establish XML as a universal best choice.

Read Table 1 and the prompt appendix before accepting the calibration or mechanistic conclusions. The appendix discloses 29.8%/45.2% empty extractions from a Gemma free-form parser bug without explaining corrected-result accounting. The confidence-elicitation conclusion contradicts Table 5, and several figure captions disagree with plotted values. Cross-group CKA pairing and sample handling are unclear; linear probes decode the model’s selected option rather than correctness, so they do not establish a causal reasoning mechanism. All 25 pages and material figures/tables were read. This is a useful schema-design hypothesis to retest on a deployment’s own tasks, not an established universal calibration rule or production guarantee.
papers.summary_zh:
要求模型輸出 JSON 或 XML，是否必然犧牲正確率？這篇研究把格式與欄位順序分開，比較先推理後回答、先回答後解釋及自由文字，涵蓋五個模型、四項基準，並延伸至信心校準與隱藏表徵。主要價值是提醒開發者：答案何時生成，可能比包在哪種格式裡更重要。

表一的二十組模型與任務中，推理優先格式拿下十三組最佳結果。GSM8K 上，Llama 與 Gemma 的 XML 答案優先正確率同為 10.98%，推理優先則為 83.53% 與 87.06%；但 LogicBench 三個模型仍由答案優先取勝，SQL 任務也有退步，不能歸納成 XML 永遠較好。

建議先看表一和附錄提示，再讀校準與機理主張。附錄承認 Gemma 自由文字解析器有 29.8%／45.2% 空抽取，卻未交代修正後如何重算；信心比較的文字結論與表五相反，部分圖說也不符圖內數字。CKA 的跨組配對及樣本數處理不清，線性探針預測的是模型選項而非答案正確性，不足以證明推理因果機制。全文二十五頁與圖表已讀。這是值得在自身任務重測的格式設計線索，尚非已確立的全面校準法則或生產環境保證。

llm_evaluation.rationale: A strong alignment-methodology contribution: broad single-value interventions turn value interaction into a testable prediction target, and behavioral/activation representations substantially outperform descriptions in eight matched model-training settings. Persona similarity reaches aggregate rho .45 and supports a separate 64-target robustness association plus taxonomy evaluation. Detailed data construction, disjoint DPO assignment, alternate metrics and elicitation/layer checks add credibility. Limits are substantial: rank correlation is moderate and symmetric while transfer is directional; one synthetic generation/judging ecosystem underlies many claims; selected single-turn values exclude important hard-to-generate risks; and the robustness study is observational within one model and attack format. Two model families and cross-model ARI .24 support partial shared structure, not a universal value space. Code/data are linked but not independently retrieved or reproduced.

primary_link.title: Predicting Alignment Generalization with Value Representations

papers.summary: LLM developers post-train their models to exhibit prosocial values and behavioral traits, which are enumerated in an alignment target. However, while recent post-training developments have yielded models that score highly on alignment evaluations, training models on sets of narrow behaviors still influences their behavior across unseen contexts and environments in unexpected ways. In this paper, we establish the task of alignment generalization prediction, i.e., predicting how fine-tuning a model to follow a given value changes its behavior across a wide range of held-out values. We conduct a large-scale analysis of alignment generalization effects across 66 values found in modern alignment targets, and benchmark representational techniques on the alignment generalization prediction task. We find that representations based on model activations when applying values in context significantly outperform methods based on textual descriptions of the values. Specifically, the best activations-based methods achieve correlations of 0.45 with our generalization matrix, compared with 0.05 from description-based baselines. We then show the applicability of representations that predict alignment generalization toward downstream tasks by using them to measure how similar the values in a multi-value alignment target are, which we find is significantly correlated with model robustness. Finally, we show initial evidence towards a shared, model-independent value space, which we use to develop the first taxonomy of LLM values grounded in empirical generalization dynamics. Our work demonstrates the importance of studying value generalization in LLMs and its application toward the more empirical design and training of model behavior.
papers.summary_en: Across four Olmo/Qwen models and SFT/DPO, persona-vector similarities predict cross-value training effects with aggregate Spearman rho .45, versus .05 for description embeddings. Coherence also correlates with prefill robustness in 64 six-value Qwen fine-tunes, and ValueMap clusters 266 values. These are useful empirical proxies, not calibrated safety predictions: synthetic judging, selected single-turn values, shared pipelines and limited model families constrain causal and universal claims.
papers.summary_zh: 把模型訓練得更誠實、體貼或謹慎，會如何改變它在其他價值衝突中的選擇？本文把這個問題整理成「對齊泛化預測」任務，從66項行為價值建立衝突情境，以四個Olmo與Qwen基礎模型進行單一價值SFT與DPO訓練，再測量對其他價值的轉移。公平比較採兩種訓練共有的49項來源價值，形成49乘66矩陣。研究比較文字描述、行為文字、權重差、人格向量與梯度方向，發現以正反價值回應的內部活化差形成的人格向量，與轉移矩陣的Spearman相關為0.45，高於描述嵌入的0.05；這是中度排序相關，不是45%的預測準確率。在64組、每組六項價值的Qwen微調中，人格向量的一致性也與抗預填干擾能力相關，但未證明提高一致性會造成安全提升。作者另將266項價值聚成四類，較既有分類貼近實測轉移結構。此方法有助於在昂貴訓練前篩查可能的價值連動；仍受合成情境、共用裁判、兩個模型家族及單回合可對比價值的選擇限制。跨模型幾何相似不等於相同價值本體，分類一致度也僅中等，不能外推到長期代理行為、所有風險或完整人類價值。

links.title: Runnable Commit Untangling for Coding Agents

evidence: pp.3–4, Section 2.2 and Figure 1: every change appears exactly once, sequential commits reconstruct the original final code, and runnability means pytest can discover/load tests; functional correctness is separate and an unrunnable final patch is incompatible with the constraints.

pp.5–6, Section 3.1 and Figure 2: a plan is structurally validated, applied and collection-checked; errors trigger reordering, at most two new agent revision sessions, then adjacent merging; git bisect supplies a candidate commit for repair.

pp.6–7, Section 3.2 and Equation 1: report reconstruction, version/history runnability, intermediate test failures, commit counts and MTP/TPE test-gain proxies; repair success requires both target fixes and preservation of previously passing evaluation tests.

pp.8–9, Section 4.1 and Figure 3: RQ1 has 131 completed Opus-generated patches from 100 Python repositories; RQ2 has 453 regression patches from 108 tasks/90 repositories and six generators, selected using later recovery; 150 samples come from 434 eligible histories with at least four commits and completed bisect.

pp.9–10, Sections 4.2–4.3: all three LLM untanglers use DeepSeek-V4-Flash; Atomizer is adapted to Python with bge-base-en-v1.5 and 0.6 similarity threshold; mini-swe-agent 2.4.6, 80 steps/session/repair, temperature 0, top-p 1; main repairs have three attempts, extra models one.

p.11, Table 1: RucTangle reconstructs 131/131, all-version runnability 100%, mean/median commits 8.64/8, singleton 0.8%, mean ITF .017, no-ITF histories 82.3%, MTP .552 and TPE .562; runnable does not mean no temporary functional failures.
p.11, Section 5.1: average untangling time 276.3 seconds and 11.9K output tokens; time includes constructing/checking/revising histories but excludes bisect and repair.

p.12, Table 2: on 453 patches and three attempts per condition, NoHistory→RucTangle Qwen pass@1 26.9→31.3 and pass@3 40.4→43.5; Nemotron 30.8→36.0 and 41.1→47.7; failed untangling conditions reuse corresponding NoHistory outcomes.

pp.12–13, Table 3: 150-patch one-attempt pass@1 is MiMo 29.3→36.0, Qwen3.7 50.0→53.3, DeepSeek 61.3→61.3 and GPT-6-Luna 50.0→48.7; GPT-6-Luna uses reasoning effort none. Five models more often introduce new regressions (Section 5.2).

pp.13–14, Section 5.3: selected poethepoet and pydantic-xml trajectories illustrate diffs and messages helping identify/preserve behavior, but a misleading generated message can make an agent doubt a correct repair until its step budget is exhausted.

pp.14–15, Section 6.1 and Table 4: Nemotron original→halved histories on the shared 150 patches lower pass@1 34.9→31.8 and increase new regressions 25.6→28.4; both include bisect and three attempts; merging also changes messages and localized change scope.

pp.16–19, Sections 6.3–8 and References: Python/SWE-CI scope, Atomizer adaptation and unisolated bisect effects are acknowledged; human benefits and other languages remain unevaluated; the PDF ends with references, with no in-file appendix.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant agent-maintenance study that moves commit untangling from syntactic grouping toward executable histories and downstream repair. Its strongest result is full pytest-collection runnability on the 131 selected Python patches while retaining a median eight commits. On 453 regression patches, history plus bisect raises Qwen/Nemotron pass@1 by 4.4/5.2 percentage points. Credit is limited by bundled localization, selected recoverable regressions, mixed extra-model outcomes, increased collateral failures, absent uncertainty estimates and unverified implementation availability. This supports a promising bounded workflow, not universal repository safety or isolated proof that finer commits cause the repair gains.

primary_link.title: Runnable Commit Untangling for Coding Agents

papers.summary: Coding agents produce large, tangled patches that mix multiple development purposes, making the code hard to review and maintain. Commit untangling offers the promise of organizing such large patches into untangled, manageable commits. This paper emphasizes two important limitations in existing commit untangling studies. First, they do not consider that untangled commits are ordered and should leave the code runnable. In practice, maintainers are unlikely to accept commits that prevent the code from running. Second, existing studies claim that commit untangling helps software maintenance. However, they conduct syntactic comparisons between the untangled commits and developers' original commits without directly showing the claimed maintenance benefits. To address these gaps, this paper makes two novel contributions: (1) RucTangle, the first agentic method that untangles commits while keeping the code runnable after each commit; and (2) TangleEval, the first evaluation framework that quantifies how untangled, manageable commit histories help coding agents repair bugs. We compare RucTangle against four untangling methods on 131 agent-generated patches. All histories produced by RucTangle are runnable, while baselines produce 20.6%-37.4% unrunnable commit histories. We further collect 453 agent-generated patches that introduce regressions (i.e., causing previously passing tests to fail) and ask two other coding agents to repair regressions. Augmenting agent context with RucTangle-produced histories yields 5.2% absolute improvement in pass@1. We also analyze agent trajectories to learn how they use untangled commits to navigate and fix bugs. Our findings demonstrate the value of adopting established software engineering practices in the era of coding agents, which broaden the future research agenda: how can agents actively use software history to make better development decisions?
papers.summary_en: RucTangle splits coding-agent patches into ordered commits, revising or merging them until pytest can collect tests without changing final code. All 131 sampled Python patches passed this check. On 453 regression patches, histories plus git bisect raised Qwen/Nemotron pass@1 from 26.9/30.8% to 31.3/36.0%. Extra-model results were mixed, and new regressions often increased. Collection is not correctness; selected data and bundled localization limit causal and cross-repository claims.
papers.summary_zh: 程式代理常把修錯、重構與新增功能混在大型補丁中，讓後續維護難以追查。RucTangle先按目的分組並安排提交順序，再逐步套用，以pytest能否蒐集、載入測試檢查中間版本；失敗時先重排，再請代理修訂，最後合併相鄰提交，全程保留原補丁的最終程式碼。TangleEval進一步評估這些歷史能否協助修復回歸錯誤，而非只比對人工分組。在131份Python補丁上，所有輸出歷史皆通過此可執行性檢查，提交中位數為8；但這不代表功能測試全通過。在453份回歸補丁上，歷史加上git bisect定位，讓Qwen與Nemotron的pass@1分別由26.9%、30.8%升至31.3%、36.0%。額外四模型則兩升、一平、一降，且多數模型更常引入新錯誤。研究價值在於把可維護的提交歷史納入代理評測；限制是只涵蓋SWE-CI的Python專案、樣本偏向曾恢復的回歸，未拆開歷史與定位的效益，也未證實真人審查或任意儲存庫皆受益。生成的提交訊息仍可能誤導修復，須以程式碼與測試交叉核對。

llm_evaluation.rationale: A directly relevant safety-evaluation audit with a useful shift from leaderboard totals to explicitly scoped measurement claims. The most convincing evidence is the five-split predictive advantage of prespecified response-process factors over the strongest fitted unidimensional comparator, supported by item-family and no-copyright checks. Developer DIF is conditional and mostly attenuates under finer matching; this is not a ranking of developer safety. Credit is moderated by a single convenience cohort, response-level rather than model-family holdouts, dependent lineages, strict judge-score binarization, and the lack of an original-HarmBench scoring replication. Bernoulli-null eigenvalues and improved multidimensional prediction cannot by themselves establish substantive constructs or their causal existence. Code is linked and estimation details supplied, but access and results were not independently reproduced.

primary_link.title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark

papers.summary: Safety benchmarks typically report one overall score for a suite of datasets, each of which may target one or more safety-related attributes, so models with similar overall scores can have very different attribute profiles. Comparing models is more tractable at the level of individual attributes, yet it is often unclear whether even a single dataset's scores isolate any single attribute. One plausible candidate for such an attribute is harmful refusal, a model's tendency to refuse dangerous or policy-violating prompts. We examine whether it constitutes a single, measurable attribute in HELM Safety. Using a construct validity framework that stipulates that an attribute must exist before a test can measure it, we start with HELM Safety's four datasets that might plausibly target harmful refusal, but find that three are saturated. We subject the remaining dataset, HarmBench, to two psychometric tests to determine if a single attribute like harmful refusal could stand behind its score. First, multidimensional item response theory modeling strongly suggests that HarmBench does not measure a singular attribute. Second, a differential item functioning analysis finds items where models from different developers with the same refusal ability score differently. These flags largely disappear under scope-specific matching, a pattern consistent with aggregation effects but not sufficient to rule out domain-specific developer differences. Zooming out, HarmBench collapses distinct harm behaviors into one score, and the overall HELM safety aggregate further collapses HarmBench and scores from other datasets into a single top-line number. Any safety score that averages over datasets and items can hide saturation and conflate behaviors this way. We argue that a score should earn its single-attribute reading before models are compared with it.
papers.summary_en: An audit of 81 HELM Safety models finds three refusal datasets near saturation and examines 398 HarmBench items. A three-factor IRT model improves held-out log-loss from the strongest one-factor comparator’s 0.322 to 0.258. Developer DIF flags largely shrink after scope-specific matching. This supports reporting behavioral profiles, but shared model lineages, judge-based binarization and response-level splits limit generalization; statistical dimensions do not establish causal constructs.
papers.summary_zh: 安全排行榜的一個總分，是否真能代表模型拒絕有害請求的單一能力？本文稽核HELM Safety的81個模型，發現四個相關資料集中有三個通過率達92%至94%，難以區分這批模型，因此進一步分析HarmBench的398題。研究先把兩位語言模型裁判的分數嚴格二值化，再比較單維、多維與按題型分組的項目反應模型。五次回應層級切分中，區分直接請求、情境請求及版權題的三維模型，測試對數損失為0.258，優於最強單維比較的0.322；移除版權題後仍有較小的多維優勢。另將OpenAI與Anthropic模型按估計能力配對，單一總分下的13個差異試題標記，在分題型後降至1個，但這不能證明開發者差異消失。價值在於提醒讀者把安全分數拆回具體行為，而非把總分當普遍安全保證。限制包括模型家族相依、裁判偏差、嚴格門檻丟失資訊，以及測試集仍共享相同模型與題目。結果僅適用這次HELM評分方式，未驗證HarmBench原始流程；多維擬合也未證明精確構念數、因果機制或拒絕能力不存在。

links.title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff

evidence: pp.1–3, Abstract/Introduction and Figures 1–2: proposed strong Allee effect is a minimal toy-theory prediction. The paper explicitly disclaims quantitatively precise real-world population predictions (p.3). No new observed runaway population is reported.

p.4, Definition 1 and unnumbered symbol table; p.5 Figure 3: N counts active AI systems able to contribute to establishing further units, not machines, API calls or weight copies. A controller and its internal subagents may constitute one unit; population configuration mix is held fixed.

p.5, Equations 1–5: independent expected growth is N(kappa*q-mu)/tau; collaborative growth is N(kappa*p(N)-mu)/tau; the success threshold is mu/kappa. The baseline does not have a population threshold when individual q is fixed.

pp.6–7, Equations 6–14 and Figure 4: successful joint attempts add kappa*N units, losses are mu*N, resources and loss rates are size-independent, remaining unsuccessful tasks decay exponentially with search depth, and exhaustive effective search cost grows exponentially. The depth-survival assumption is not implied merely by a search tree.

p.8, Equations 15–17 and Figure 5: pooled work proportional to N gives p(N)=1-(1-pref)*(N/Nref)^(-beta). Power-law work N^alpha changes the effective exponent to alpha*rho/ln(B). These are assumptions, not measured universal scaling laws.

pp.8–9, Figure 6: redrawn math pass-rate/test-time-compute data motivates a local logarithmic relationship but does not establish equivalence of compute and population size or success at adding active units.

p.9, Equation 18: for pref<pcrit<1 and beta>0, Ncrit=Nref*((1-pref)/(1-pcrit))^(1/beta). If kappa<=mu there is no positive growth; if pref=pcrit the reference is marginal (zero instantaneous growth), rather than strictly positive.

p.10, Figure 7: illustrative Nref=16, pref=.10, pcrit=.20 and beta=.035 give Ncrit approximately 463. This is a model-dependent example, not an empirical bound; panel c explicitly uses single-agent Nref=1 and must not share the panel-a normalization implicitly.
pp.10–11, Sections 3.2/4: ecological red teaming and population pacing are proposed; current population proximity to a threshold is explicitly unknown and requires population-scaling observations.
p.16, Appendix A Equations 19–27: exact finite-depth correction increases the threshold for pref<pcrit and finite B^dref relative to the large-depth approximation; it vanishes as B^dref grows.

pp.17–20, Appendix B Equations 28–41 and Figures 8–10: sublinear alpha=.72 shifts the illustration to about 1714; saturation with N0=1500 requires beta>about .0259 and gives about550; unavoidable congestion requires beta>about .0332 and permits growth only between about761 and2610. Idling/partitioning surplus units invalidates the assumed unavoidable-congestion mechanism.

pp.20–22, Appendix C, Table 1 and Figure 11: GPT-5.6 Sol related-task data uses N=1/4/16 and five effort levels. SEC-Bench Pro beta=.025/.044/.043/.027/.069; BrowseComp=.328/.214/.155/.157/.113. Nine fits have RMSE<=1.67%; SEC High has4.59%. No trial counts or standard errors are available.

p.21 and Figure11(c–d), p.22: normalized output-token exponents are .49–.60 (SEC) and .66–.90 (BrowseComp); pooled .54/.72. Tokens may duplicate work and are not C(N); three-count fits cannot establish a population-expansion scaling law.
pp.12–15: all 53 references were read as bibliographic content. Cited external incidents, deployment counts, websites and datasets were not fetched or independently verified during this review.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant conceptual contribution to agent safety: explicit active-unit accounting makes population size a separate evaluation axis, and the conditional threshold is transparent. Its strength is analytical clarity and sensitivity analysis, not demonstrated real-world takeoff. The main mechanism assumes population-proportional additions, fixed losses/resources/composition, and an increasing pooled-work success law. Saturation can remove a finite threshold, and unavoidable congestion can bound growth. Three-count related-task fits without uncertainty do not identify an end-to-end expansion law or a safe deployment size. Extreme-congestion probability validity and stochastic extinction are unresolved. The score therefore credits the safety framing and derivations while substantially discounting empirical strength and transfer.

llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這是高度相關的代理安全概念研究：活動單位的明確核算，讓族群大小成為獨立評測軸，條件式門檻也容易檢驗。優點是解析清楚與敏感度分析，不能當成已證明真實族群起飛。核心依賴按人口比例新增、固定流失／資源／組成，以及有效工作提高成功率；飽和可能消除有限門檻，不可避免的壅塞則可限制增長。三種代理數的相關任務擬合缺不確定性，無法識別端到端擴張規律或安全部署規模；極端壅塞的機率有效域及隨機滅絕也未解決。因此給予安全問題設定與推導較高評價，對經驗證據及跨環境適用性保留。

scope_assessment.reason: Language-model agent population safety and collaboration scaling; ecological concepts are methodological, not a biological-domain application.

primary_link.title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff

papers.summary: AI agents can now conduct real-world cyberattacks, scale up capabilities with the number of agents, and collectively pursue misaligned goals to obtain rewards. Together, these factors raise the risk of a population explosion of misaligned agents: agents could compromise computers and secretly deploy additional agents, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where larger populations develop greater collective cyber capability and expand further. This raises a fundamental question: What determines whether a population of misaligned agents remains contained or takes off into this self-reinforcing cycle? This population-level problem is ecological safety: unlike individual-agent or multi-agent safety with a fixed population, it concerns the dynamics of the population itself. Here, we develop an ecological theory of AI-agent populations based on a population growth equation in which fitness (growth rate) depends on cybersecurity capability. We show that, without collaboration, the population takes off only when individual-agent capability exceeds a critical threshold. With collaboration, however, collective cybersecurity capability increases with population size. This creates a critical population threshold: below it, the population declines; above it, the population takes off, even though individual-agent capability has not changed. In ecology, this phenomenon is known as the strong Allee effect. Because red teaming a small group of agents cannot guarantee ecological safety in larger populations, our theory calls for ecological red teaming and population pacing: gradually deploying larger agent populations in controlled environments, while measuring how cyber capability scales with population size, and estimating the critical population size for takeoff. Capability gains may lower this threshold, requiring re-estimation for each new model generation.
papers.summary_en: Can a safe small group of AI agents become an unsafe large population without improving any individual model? This paper builds a minimal ecological model that counts active systems capable of helping establish further units. Independent attempts yield growth only above an individual-success threshold. If collaboration increases collective success and successful attempts add units in proportion to population size, a strong Allee effect can instead produce a critical population threshold. A search-depth model gives a power-law decrease in failure probability and an analytic threshold. Appendices examine finite-depth corrections, sublinear work, saturation and unavoidable congestion; the latter can restrict growth to an intermediate population range. The authors propose controlled population scaling and ecological red teaming. These are conditional theoretical results, not observations of runaway populations or a calibrated deployment limit. The roughly 463-agent illustration depends on chosen parameters and a 16-agent reference population. Related benchmark fits use only one, four and sixteen agents at five effort settings, do not measure establishment of new active units, and lack reported trial counts and standard errors. Fixed resource availability, loss rates and population composition further limit transfer. The work offers a useful safety-evaluation lens, while leaving real-world thresholds, stochastic extinction risk and empirical validation unresolved.
papers.summary_zh: 少量AI代理通過安全測試，是否足以保證大規模部署安全？本文把可持續參與擴張的活動系統視為族群單位，以新增與流失的差額描述人口變化。獨立行動時，增長取決於單體成功率；協作時，若群體能共享搜尋成果、成功率隨數量提高，即使單體能力不變，也可能跨越由衰退轉為增長的臨界規模，形成強阿利效應。作者把搜尋深度的成功機率、指數搜尋成本及有效工作量的冪次增長結合，推導門檻公式，並提出逐步擴大受控測試、同時量測新增能力與終止率的生態紅隊評估。附錄進一步說明，通訊瓶頸可能使增長永遠無法發生；不可避免的協調壅塞則可能只允許中等規模增長。然而，這是條件式理論模型，不是已觀察到失控代理族群。圖中約463個代理的門檻只是特定參數示例；相關基準僅有1、4、16個代理與五種推理強度，既不直接測試建立新活動單位，也缺試驗次數與誤差範圍。其價值在於指出固定規模評測的盲點；固定資源、損失率與組成假設、少量資料及未校準的真實環境，均限制部署門檻的實用性。

links.title: Chronos Enables Code Agents to Reason over Software Evolution

evidence: pp.1–4, Figures1–2: Merged PR title/body/discussion/patch distilled by Qwen3.5-Plus into Summary, Signals, Motivation and Solution. Summary is the embedding anchor; Signals has12–20 cues; Solution has1–3 annotated code patterns and3–5 pitfalls. Figure1 mixes backbones/scaffolds and provides context, not a controlled leaderboard comparison.

pp.5–6, Table1: Eleven relation families span code, developer-intent and organizational tiers. Precedes requires file Jaccard≥.5 with w=.5+overlap in[1,1.5]; extends uses1; follows uses .7+.35(t+d)/2 in[.7,1.05]; social overlap weights span[.3,.45]. Follows coverage~73% versus precedes~62% measures node coverage, not marginal usefulness.

p.7, Equations1–2: DashScope text-embedding-v4 is2048D; filter initial10K candidates then retain K semantic entries; a=max(0,cos). Expanded score=a exp(−h/3)(1+sum edge weights), maximum over explored paths. Semantic entries precede up to K graph nodes; this is not global mixed-score sorting or calibrated probability.

pp.8–9, Algorithm1: H=3 and B=200 by default; nodes already on the current path are skipped. Nodes must match repository and have creation/merge before the target PR creation cutoff; filename filters constrain entry and traversal. Parallel typed edges are alternative routes, not summed associations. Maximum is over bounded explored paths, not a guaranteed global optimum.

pp.9–10, Table2: Change and validation agents separately produce patches; the steward randomizes X/Y and selects an existing patch without editing. Identical/one-empty/two-empty routes bypass review; invalid choice falls back to fixed-seed random selection. One final patch does not mean one candidate or equal computation.

pp.10–11, Table3: Each agent run has250 steps,$1.5 budget,200k context; K=5,H=3 returns at most10 cards. Verified has500 tasks/12 repositories; Pro public731/11; FEA Lite200/48. Six backbones are tested only on Verified; transfer uses MiniMax M2.5.

p.12, Table4: SWE-Agent→Chronos: GPT-5 Mini57.2→60.4; Claude4.5 Haiku65.6→68.4; Gemini3 Flash75.8→78.6; Kimi K2.5 71.2→74.8; Qwen3-Max69.0→75.2; MiniMax M2.5 76.4→79.8. Means69.2 and72.8667 round to69.2 and72.9; the3.6667-point gain rounds to3.7.

pp.12–13, Table5: Same MiniMax backbone: Pro48.3→51.7(+3.4pp), FEA Lite41.0→43.5(+2.5pp). Graph rules/default weights are unchanged. No repeated baseline or paired uncertainty is reported for these comparisons.

p.13, Section4.2: Full MiniMax/SWE-Agent repeated rates79.8,80.0,80.6,79.6,80.0 yield mean80.0, SD.37pp, SE.17pp, Student-t95%CI[79.5,80.5]. Baseline and other configurations use single runs; the interval is for the Chronos mean, not the method difference.

pp.13–14, Table6: Full79.8; change-only78.4; validation-only77.8; flat semantic79.0; base76.4. Mini scaffold full79.2 versus base75.8. Role removal also removes one candidate and the steward; single-agent gains include role prompting. The graph increment is.8pp, not the whole3.4pp.

pp.11–12,14, Table7/Equations3–4:100 sampled Verified tasks×10 cards; two internal expert annotators, kappa.86 before discussion adjudication. Useful: Random.18/Embedding1.24/Chronos2.87; Hit14/68/89%. These are average counts and task-hit fractions, not recall against all relevant cards.

pp.14–15, Figure3: Removing precedes reduces Useful by.60, extends.44, follows.28, references.40, backport.22, same_reviewers.18, same_discussants.08, same_milestone.14, similar_labels.10, comment mentions.12 and depends_on.06. Removal effects are conditional on other edges, not additive attribution.

pp.15–16, Section5: Weights are hand-specified with no sensitivity measurement. Build/update, embedding, adjacency inspection and card-reading costs are separate; no measured total-cost comparison is supplied. Frontiers are bounded but all outgoing edges still require inspection. Card distillation can omit/invent; usefulness annotation does not establish factuality.

pp.17–18, Sections6–7: Closest MemGovern uses structured cards and selective browsing; Chronos adds PR relations to candidate discovery. Repository Memory uses commits/issues for localization rather than the same PR-event graph. No appendices follow: pp.19–22 are references, not full prompt templates.
llm_evaluation.rationale: An actionable, highly relevant repository-memory design: structured PR cards retain rationale while typed graph expansion discovers related history beyond semantic entry matches, and the memory supports generation and selection. Six-backbone gains, two scaffolds, three benchmarks, one repeated full configuration and an explicit retrieval-quality study support usefulness. Attribution is weaker than headline gains imply: the full system generates two patches and may run a selector under per-agent rather than matched total budgets; single-agent variants also change prompts; the graph-only comparison is 79.8 versus79.0 in single runs without paired uncertainty. Human usefulness is internally judged and does not validate distilled-card factuality. Temporal filters cover entry and traversal nodes, but timestamp-consistent PR/comment snapshots and base-model contamination were not independently audited. Hand-set relation weights and limited multi-backbone transfer weaken broad claims. Full distillation and role prompts are relegated to unavailable supplements, and no implementation or data release was verified. The paper still contains enough schema, equations, pseudocode, routing and tables for a bounded analytical review, with low reproducibility and no efficiency or clean causal claim.

primary_link.title: Chronos Enables Code Agents to Reason over Software Evolution

papers.summary: Historical pull requests record the design decisions, compatibility constraints, and implementation patterns behind a codebase's current state. Experience relevant to a new task can span related changes whose descriptions emphasize different concerns. We introduce Chronos, a test-time framework that makes this connected history available to large language model (LLM)-based code agents. Chronos distills merged pull requests into structured experience cards and connects them through a typed graph of code-level, developer-intent, and organizational relations. Semantic search identifies entry cards, and weighted multi-hop expansion retrieves connected changes for selective reading. The same memory guides candidate generation and patch selection: a patch-focused change agent and a validation-strategy agent each develop a patch, and an evolution steward consults history to select between them. On SWE-Bench Verified, the full workflow improves SWE-Agent across all six evaluated LLM backbones, raising the mean resolution rate from 69.2% to 72.9% and reaching 79.8% with MiniMax M2.5. With the same backbone, it raises resolution rates from 48.3% to 51.7% on SWE-Bench Pro and from 41.0% to 43.5% on FEA-Bench Lite. Both experience-guided single-agent variants also outperform the base agent. In a human evaluation on 100 tasks with ten cards retrieved per task, graph-grounded retrieval increases the mean number of useful cards from 1.24 to 2.87 over flat semantic retrieval. These results demonstrate the value of PR relations for retrieving useful repository experience and of the evaluated workflows for applying that experience during patch generation and selection.
papers.summary_en: Chronos links PR experience cards through typed relations, then supplies retrieved history to patch generators and a selector. Across six backbones, mean SWE-Bench Verified resolution rises from 69.2% to 72.9%; graph retrieval adds 0.8 points over flat retrieval within the full workflow. Useful cards rise from 1.24 to 2.87 per ten in an internal study. Extra computation, single-run baselines and missing full prompts limit attribution and reproduction; temporal filtering alone is not a full leakage audit.
papers.summary_zh: 程式庫目前的樣貌告訴代理「程式怎麼寫」，歷史PR則可能解釋「為何必須這樣寫」。Chronos把已合併PR蒸餾成摘要、檢索線索、動機與解法四欄經驗卡，再以檔案延續、明確引用、作者後續工作與協作資訊等十一類關係連成圖。代理先找語意入口，再沿加權路徑擴展，最多列出十張卡供選讀；兩個不同取向的代理各提補丁，第三個角色參照歷史挑選其一。SWE-Bench Verified六個模型的平均解題率由69.2%升至72.9%，最強設定為79.8%；另兩項基準也各提升3.4與2.5個百分點。但完整流程含額外生成與選擇，不能把全部增益歸給圖。保留同一流程而改成平面語意檢索時為79.0%，圖本身的此項差距只有0.8個百分點，且未報配對不確定性。100題內部人工評讀中，每十卡的有用卡數由1.24增至2.87，支持檢索品質改善，但不代表卡片內容已查證無誤。優點是把可重用歷史記憶與代理分離，並在搜尋及擴展都套用時間限制。限制包括手訂權重、成本未完整量測、多數設定單次執行與內部標註偏差；完整蒸餾和角色提示補件未取得，因此能評估本文報告的流程與證據，不能宣稱已精確重現或排除所有歷史資料洩漏。

llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant benchmark contribution: swapping closely related instructions against human recordings probes whether a judge checks the exact contract rather than merely recognizing a finished workflow. The reviewed accounting, fixed scoring denominators and model-harness comparisons are useful, and class-specific accuracy reveals consequential asymmetries hidden by a leaderboard scalar. The 80.9% result is a reported configuration score on a model-defined hard subset, not evidence of reliable deployment or a statistically established model ranking. Tool-versus-direct comparisons confound representation, context and harness; no independent human agreement or score uncertainty is reported, and earlier pilot exposure weakens unseen-test claims. Table9 ablation counts do not match final AH denominators, while pair grouping across hard/easy partitions is incompletely specified. External row manifests, annotation calibration, framework instructions and environment pins were not retrieved, so release and label-level reproducibility remain unverified.

primary_link.title: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks

papers.summary: Computer-use agents are capable of completing complex tasks, increasing the use of automatic judges to determine success, either for training or for evaluation without human involvement. Despite their flexibility, their reliability on long tasks spanning multiple applications remains unclear. A trajectory, composed of long sequences of screenshots and actions, may appear complete, but in reality violates constraints from the instruction or introduces an unwanted side effect. To identify these errors, a judge needs to examine the trajectory with respect to the user's instruction. To this end, we introduce AgentHorizon, a benchmark of 1,373 computer-use tasks (instruction-trajectory pairs) drawn from 166 hours of human-recorded trajectories spanning three operating systems. By recording trajectories for closely related instructions, we can construct negative tasks by swapping the instructions. This paired design evaluates judges on their ability to distinguish a successful trajectory from one that completed a similar (but incompatible) request. We release the benchmark under three splits: a frontier split, AgentHorizon (AH), a simplified split, AgentHorizon-Simple (AH-S), and a development split, AgentHorizon-Development (AH-D). We further evaluate eleven judges by (1) directly passing the full trajectory (with up to 300 screenshots and actions), and (2) using them as coding agents across five agent harnesses. We find that our best agentic judge, GPT-5.5, achieves 80.9% balanced accuracy on the AH subset. We find that tool-use improves certain models but results in worse performance for open-weight models, and that judges differ drastically in their ability to accept a valid trajectory and reject failed ones. Our findings highlight the need for judges that are capable of locating and verifying often hidden evidence that a task was properly completed inside long interaction histories.
papers.summary_en: AgentHorizon tests whether judges notice instruction mismatches in plausible desktop workflows: 1,373 reviewed pairs derive from 850 human recordings. GPT-5.5 with Codex scores 80.9% balanced accuracy on the 528-item hard subset, with 71.8% positive accuracy. Tools help some configurations and hurt others. Curated near-misses, pilot exposure, absent independent annotator agreement and unclear ablation cohorts limit generalization and causal claims.
papers.summary_zh: 一段電腦操作看似順利完成，仍可能選錯物件、違反細節，或多做未授權的外部動作。AgentHorizon用人類錄製的相近任務交換指令，讓相同操作在不同要求下成為成功或失敗案例，測試裁判是否真的核對使用者意圖。審查後共有1,373個指令與軌跡配對，來自850份錄製，涵蓋三種作業系統；其中528題構成依三個模型判定的較難子集。GPT-5.5搭配Codex在此子集的平衡準確率為80.9%，但對有效操作的接受率只有71.8%，不可把總分當可靠部署保證。工具的效果也不一致：GPT-5.5比直接評判好，Qwen 3.6 27B卻由直接模式77.6%降至OpenCode模式70.4%；這比較同時改變提示與執行框架，不能單獨歸因於工具。研究的實用價值是把「做出了成果」與「完整遵守要求」分開，並要求查看錯誤類型及正負樣本表現。限制在人工設計的近似錯誤不代表所有真實失敗、早期開發曾接觸部分資料、缺獨立標註者一致度，以及沒有排名不確定區間。外部資料與完整校準文件未取，附錄消融的樣本數也與主測試集不同，故本次只能評議論文所報證據，未獨立重跑基準。

llm_evaluation.rationale: A relevant systems study whose most defensible contribution is measuring concrete defects in LLM-extracted policy bindings and showing how a small schema-based pass repairs or rejects them. Frozen-pool ablations, separate compliance rules, checker audits, safe-completion metrics and disclosed adverse utility outcomes strengthen the diagnosis. The guarantee remains narrow: hand-authored predicate evaluators and static tables provide much of the semantics; checks neither prove clause fidelity nor global deadlock freedom. Reported violation reductions apply only to encoded clauses and a changed population of executed writes, while the reference checker shares at least one semantic error with the gate. Zero benchmark ASR omits injection-induced payments to known payees and some destructive actions outside the benchmark flag. AgentDojo policies and vocabulary were developed with suite knowledge, and large Slack/workspace utility losses constrain use. The proprietary compiler, prompt, tables, preflight and runtime evaluators are withheld; the unacquired companion cannot be treated as reproduced evidence. This supports a bounded paper-level mechanism review, not independently validated performance or deployment certification.

primary_link.title: NOMOS: Compiling Written Policies into Statically Verified Tool-Call Gates for LLM Agents

papers.summary: Tool-using LLM agents violate the policies they are deployed to enforce, often silently. Prior defenses hand-write rules, query an LLM verifier per action, or compile policies through heavyweight formal machinery. Naive compilation fails: extracted rules block the tool satisfying their own precondition, or read arguments their tool lacks. NOMOS, a four-pass compiler, turns a natural-language policy into a deterministic tool-call gate; static verification with tool-schema-level checks alone (no prover, solver, or LLM) repairs or rejects 37% (airline) and 13% (retail) of candidates, without which most shipped rules are inoperable. Replaying compiled rules over undefended transcripts flags bindings that refuse legitimate work (a development binding refused 95.9% of task-passing calls); no evaluation binding is flagged. On $\tau^2$-bench the gate cuts violations of reference-encoded clauses among state-changing calls from 66.3% to 2.6% (airline) and 30.8% to 6.9% (retail), raising airline task success significantly for $2 \le k \le 4$; a 26B on-premise compilation is not significantly worse than hand-written or frontier-compiled rules. Unlike AgentDojo's shipped defenses, it reaches a zero attack success rate (ASR) on banking, where nine attack families collapse onto three structural rules. On the other three suites its ASR is at most 3.6%, from goals with no tool call to govern and one write admitted by a binding weaker than its clause; a second agent model, Llama-3.3-70B, reproduces the effect on both benchmarks. Decisions take microseconds without an LLM call, at a domain-dependent benign-utility cost; compilation runs on-premise on open-weight gemma-4-26B.
papers.summary_en: NOMOS binds policy clauses to a human-built predicate vocabulary, checks structural defects, then gates tool calls without a runtime LLM. Reported encoded-clause violations fall sharply, but this is neither semantic verification nor complete policy coverage. Zero banking ASR coexists with injection-induced payments to known payees; Slack benign utility falls from 90.5% to 14.3%. Withheld evaluators, prompts and tables prevent independent reproduction from the paper.

primary_link.title: Who Verifies the Verifier? Co-Evolving Inspectable Graders with Self-Improving Agents

papers.summary: We changed the agent: did it actually get better? Every self-improving agent loop answers this hundreds of times, and every answer comes from a verifier. On open-ended tasks none exists, so the loop is handed a hand-written rubric or a bare LLM judge grading output from a model like itself, inviting reward hacking and shared blind spots. We make the verifier the evolving object: an inspectable expression over small, mostly deterministic drawback detectors, synthesized from clustered failures, gated at birth, and selected for agreement with a ten-item anchored reference set plus consensus over unlabeled outputs, never for the agent's score. On MBPP+ it gains +0.21 held-out agreement over the hand-authored seed composition, on every seed, and ends ahead of the bare LLM judge it contains. One finding should change how co-evolved verifiers are validated: removing the anchor guards collapses the verifier into a vacuous always-pass grader, yet that collapsed verifier trains skills just as well. Downstream task score cannot certify a self-evolved verifier. Score does answer sufficiency, and there an evolved verifier can substitute: Double Ratchet, pairing the verifier with a lifecycle-managed skill loop, retains 88-110% of the lift that ground truth or a rubric buys the same loop, across code generation, enterprise text-to-SQL, and reference-free report generation. When evolved skills gamed the report rubric, an outer judge caught it and one added detector repaired it; the judge itself was wrong until given the task contract.
papers.summary_en: This study evolves readable verifiers from ten anchored examples and detector consensus. MBPP+ agreement rises from .417 to a .625 peak, without task-clustered significance. Crucially, an almost always-pass verifier still trains useful skills, so task success cannot certify its grader. Small samples, test-based rollback, one model family and a post-hoc report judge limit the claims; the report repair changes both a detector and its hints.
